newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan investment in China up 12 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan investment in China up 12 pct in 1996.

text.p: Taiwan's indirect investment in China rose 12 percent to US$1.229 billion in 1996 from 1995 despite Taipei's go-slow appeals to reduce political exposure in the rival mainland, officials said on Friday.
The number of China projects approved by Taiwan's Investment Commission fell 22 percent in 1996 to 383, the commission said.
The decline in the numbers of approvals "indicates that Taiwan investors in the mainland have gradually turned cautious and conservative," the commission concluded in a statement.

New China investments focussed mainly on Jiangsu, Guangdong and Hebei provinces, with major investments in electronics and electrical appliances, basic metals, food processing and chemicals manufacturing, it said.
Taiwan still bans direct investment and trade with China, its rival since the end of a civil war in 1949.

Despite the deep political divide, some 30,000 Taiwan businesses have poured over US$20 billion into the mainland, making Taiwan one of China's leading overseas investors -- and China one of Taiwan's most important markets.
In a strategic shift from the second half of 1996, Taiwan's Nationalist government has warned that the island's economy must not become overdependent on the communist mainland.
Taipei has urged firms to reconsider investments in China and invest more in Taiwan or other overseas destinations.
Several major Taiwan firms have called off or postponed major China investments in apparent compliance with the appeal.
Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province that must ultimately be reunified with the mainland, and reserves a right to use force to thwart any Taiwan move toward independence.
